summary: Preserved the candidate's dedicated DP health routing, which isolates user round-robin and load-budget state, but rejected its synthetic idle success. Idle /health_generate probes again enter generation admission so success requires a model result; busy probes still piggyback without admission. The candidate's MagicMock scheduler test was corrected to test this contract and is not presented as distributed PrefillDelayer evidence.

tests.command: source inspection and regression comparison at f8853833a75e992e618a9e5d74efe493c3bfefe2
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: candidate process_input_requests appends an idle probe IPC, calls maybe_send_health_check_signal immediately, and continues before _request_dispatcher; therefore HTTP success requires no generation/model forward. The revised idle-admission regression has the opposite required assertion.
28 passed: idle probe enters generation admission; busy probe bypasses it; health routing does not consume user round-robin state or refresh user load budgets.

gpu_evidence: No GPU claim was needed for the deterministic control-flow correction. The assigned environment is one AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950, not 8 NVIDIA B30Z, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro weights are unavailable.
remaining_limitations: No TP8/DP8 DeepSeek-V4-Pro run on 8x NVIDIA B30Z was possible, so elimination of the reported LOW throughput regime, 16,384-token divergence, persistent mixed/delay state, and running-request collapse remains unverified.

An idle real generation probe can participate in scheduler admission and therefore cannot simultaneously be claimed to leave all real distributed PrefillDelayer state unchanged. The change only proves DP routing-state isolation and preserves genuine model/device health coverage.
The focused test uses a mocked dispatcher only to establish admission versus bypass and makes no distributed synchronization claim.
